name: MonarchPasswordStrengthMeter
title: PasswordStrengthMeter
summary: Shows how strong a password is while it is typed: a four-part bar, the strength in words, and each requirement as met or not met.
whenToUse: Under a MonarchPasswordInput with purpose New, on sign-up and password reset screens.
whenNotToUse: On a sign-in screen, where the password already exists. For a general measure use MonarchProgress.
api: @Composable fun MonarchPasswordStrengthMeter(password: String, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, rules: List<MonarchPasswordRule> = MonarchPasswordRule.defaults(), showRules: Boolean = true, score: ((String) -> MonarchPasswordStrength)? = null, labels: MonarchPasswordStrengthMeterLabels = MonarchPasswordStrengthMeterLabels())

class MonarchPasswordRule(id: String, label: String, test: (String) -> Boolean) { companion object { const val DEFAULT_MIN_LENGTH: Int = 8; fun defaults(length: String, case: String, number: String, symbol: String): List<MonarchPasswordRule>; @Composable fun defaults(): List<MonarchPasswordRule> } }

enum class MonarchPasswordStrength { VeryWeak, Weak, Fair, Good, Strong; companion object { const val STRONG_LENGTH: Int = 14; fun score(password: String, rules: List<MonarchPasswordRule>): MonarchPasswordStrength } }
class MonarchPasswordStrengthMeterLabels(strengthText: ((MonarchPasswordStrength?) -> String)? = null, rulesLabel: String? = null, ruleText: ((label: String, met: Boolean) -> String)? = null)

options.name: password
options.description: The password to rate. It is only read; nothing is stored.

options.name: rules
options.description: The requirements listed and counted by the default score: at least 8 characters, upper and lower case, a number, a symbol or space. An empty list hides the list.

options.name: score
options.description: A custom estimator. By default MonarchPasswordStrength.score(password, rules). Not called for an empty password.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for the strength line, the spoken name of the list ("Password requirements") and the spoken text of a rule ("Met: …", "Not met: …").

states.name: empty
states.description: No segment is filled, the line reads "Password strength: Not entered" and no rule is met.

states.name: very weak, weak
states.description: One segment in the danger solid color.

states.name: fair
states.description: Two segments in the warning solid color.

states.name: good, strong
states.description: Three or four segments in the success solid color.

states.name: rule met
states.description: A filled disc and the success strong text color; a rule not met has an empty ring and the muted text color.

appearance: Empty segments use the emphasis background; filled ones the danger, warning or success solid color. The strength line is muted caption text. A met rule is in the success strong color with a filled disc, an unmet one in the muted text color with a ring. The same roles apply in light, dark and both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: The same rules, score, levels and texts as the web and iOS. Rule tests are Kotlin lambdas; lengths count Unicode code points, as the web counts code points, so the platforms agree on the same password. The default rule labels are Android string resources, so MonarchPasswordRule.defaults() is a composable; MonarchPasswordRule.defaults(length, case, number, symbol) builds the same rules with the app's own labels outside composition. The web draws a check and a dot as the rule marks and iOS uses SF Symbols; Monarch for Android bundles no icons, so the marks are a filled disc and an empty ring drawn as shapes. Strength texts are replaced through one labels object, as on iOS, instead of the web's messages object.
accessibility: The bar is hidden from TalkBack; the strength is always a line of text.
The strength line is a polite live region, so TalkBack announces it when it changes.
Each rule is one element read as "Met: …" or "Not met: …".
Met and not met differ by the shape of the mark (filled disc or empty ring) as well as color.
The list has the spoken name "Password requirements" and collection information with one row per rule.
Text wraps at font scale 2.0; the bar keeps its height.
edgeCases: An empty password is never scored: the custom score is not called and no rule is met.
An empty rules list hides the list and makes every non-empty password at least Good with the default score.
Each change of the password announces the strength line again only when its text changes.

examples.title: With a new password
Your own rules and estimator
examples.code:
MonarchPasswordStrengthMeter(
    password = "correct horse battery",
    rules = listOf(
        MonarchPasswordRule(id = "words", label = "At least three words") { it.split(' ').size >= 3 },
    ),
    score = { if (it.length >= 20) MonarchPasswordStrength.Strong else MonarchPasswordStrength.Fair },
)
